subject: Mid-quarter mission focus: proposed scope shift & dependency roster
body:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-quarter mission focus: proposed scope shift & dependency roster

Team —

Quick mid-quarter pulse and a concrete proposal ahead of QBR prep. After reviewing usage telemetry and the evaluation set (attached), I believe we should tighten our mission focus for the next 6 weeks: prioritize latency and reliability improvements for the Redwood API over the planned feature breadth expansion for Initiative B.

Why:
- Token-level latencies on tail p95 rose 18% in Sept for conversational workloads (perf deck attached).
- Several enterprise prospects flagged SLA and cold-start variability as blockers in procurement conversations (see HubSpot notes: HUBSPOT-123456).
- We can deliver measurable customer impact faster by shifting 30% of Q4 engineering runway from Initiative B feature work to serving/runtime optimizations and caching.

What I propose (high level):
1) Re-scope Initiative B -> cut the optional UI polish and defer integration connectors to next cycle.
2) Move two backend engineers (4 wks each, contractor or FTE swap) into the serving runtime track for focused KV cache & batching improvements.
3) Request infra support: dedicated perf lab access (1 x A100 for 3 weeks), a temporary GPU quota bump, and a prioritized slot in the load-testing calendar.
4) Exec decision target: sign-off by Tue 2026-10-12 so we can align QBR narrative and finalize the QBR deck.

Dependencies I need from people on this thread:
- Neha: feasibility and ETA for perf lab + any procurement blockers.
- Vanessa: product tradeoffs and customer messaging that will go into the QBR.
- Marissa: operations—can we reprioritize two engineers and temporarily reassign them?
- Vivek: financial/SLAs—are you comfortable with the temporary capacity bump and how we present the economics?

Attachments: QBR-deck-v2.pdf (draft slides), infra-impact-worksheet.xlsx (quick cost model), mutual-action-plan.docx (initial MAP)

Short ask: please reply with green / red / needs-info by 2026-10-06 so we can iterate the deck.

Thanks,
Logan
Logan Wright
Senior Product Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

----
On Mon, 04 Oct 2026 at 10:03:00 -0700, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com> wrote:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-quarter mission focus: proposed scope shift & dependency roster

Logan —

Thanks for the crisp framing. I'm generally supportive of focusing the short runway on latency/reliability, especially given the prospect feedback. A couple clarifying asks before I can fully sign off on messaging:

1) Which customer-impact KPIs should land on the QBR front slide? I suggest p95 tail latency, cold-start percentiles, and 28-day retention impact.
2) For Initiative B: can we quantify the delta in customer-facing value if we trim the UI polish? Need a one-slide summary for the execs.

Also: workforce question — I prefer an FTE swap over contractor spend if we can shuffle resources internally for 4–6 weeks. If we move people from Growth into Infra, we should surface expected ramp time and a fallback plan.

I'll add recommended customer messaging snippets into the deck and loop in Sarah Cox (NorthBridge) for a short quote we can use as a signal if helpful (she's an exec we work with on procurement).

-V
Vanessa Ortiz
VP, Product

----
On Thu, 08 Oct 2026 at 13:41:00 -0700, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com> wrote:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Oct 2026 13:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-quarter mission focus: proposed scope shift & dependency roster

Quick infra check-in on feasibility and blockers.

Summary: possible, with caveats.
- Perf lab: we have a 3-week slot starting 2026-10-18 that can be reserved; however, it requires a signed order for temporary capacity by 2026-10-13 (procurement/finance).
- GPU quota bump: cloud provider will grant +2 A100-equivalent quota for a 30-day window, but we need an internal chargeback code and committed consumption estimate (see infra-impact-worksheet.xlsx).
- Load-testing calendar: open week of 2026-10-25; scheduling depends on the availability of the performance engineers.

Blocking items I need from the group:
1) A clear list of JIRA tickets / acceptance criteria for the perf work (please tag JIRA-INFRA-712).
2) Finance sign-off for temporary quota costs or a commitment to reallocate budget.
3) Confirmation on which two engineers (names) we would move so we can forecast ramp-day impact.

Attachment: infra-impact-worksheet.xlsx (estimates filled in)

Neha
Director, Infrastructure

----
On Sun, 10 Oct 2026 at 08:57:00 -0700, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Oct 2026 08:57:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-quarter mission focus: proposed scope shift & dependency roster

Thanks — I'm aligned with the approach if we can land the temporary resource trade cleanly. Operational asks and next steps: 

- I'll propose a mutual action plan (MAP) that documents the handoff scope and ramp checklist. Draft attached (mutual-action-plan.docx).
- Proposed engineers to move: Rajesh Iyer (Backend) and Kim Park (Serving). Both are currently in Growth squads; both have prior infra experience. They can start 2026-10-19 with a 1-week overlap in knowledge transfer.
- I'll coordinate with People/IC managers to schedule the temporary swap and capture any performance impact mitigation.
- Decision needed: Finance sign-off for GPU bump (Vivek), and Product exec messaging approval (Vanessa).

If we can get the approvals by Tue 2026-10-12, I will lock the MAP and update the QBR deck.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Ops & Launches

Attachment: mutual-action-plan.docx

----
On Sun, 11 Oct 2026 at 11:23:00 -0700, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com> wrote:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-quarter mission focus: proposed scope shift & dependency roster

Green with two conditions:
1) We define a 30-day ROI target for the GPU bump and agree on a cost cap that we can present at QBR. Neha, please add a conservative consumption estimate to the infra-impact worksheet.
2) Product needs to own a customer-facing note about the temporary scope trade and expected timelines (Vanessa).

I'll authorize the temporary quota bump once Neha and Marissa confirm the chargeback code and MAP is signed.

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Finance & Business Ops

----
Notes: Sarah Cox (NorthBridge) agreed offline to provide a short procurement comment for the QBR if we include an explicit reliability roadmap. I'll draft the QBR front slide once we lock the resource decision.

Action items summary (assigned):
- Neha: finalize procurement path and add consumption estimates (due 2026-10-13).
- Marissa: finalize MAP and confirm engineer names with managers (due 2026-10-12).
- Vanessa: customer messaging and one-slide delta on Initiative B (due 2026-10-12).
- Vivek: sign quota bump after infra estimates and MAP are in (target 2026-10-13).

--
End of thread
